title: Bhai Buddha Singh Secures the Fort at Great Cost

blocks.text: The Khalsa chiefs first decide that the stronghold must be secured before its wealth is fully apportioned. In that setting Bhai Buddha Singh emerges as the key actor, negotiating for possession while others weigh whether purchase, seizure, and political necessity can be separated at all.

The page underscores the scale of his payment and ambition: Rupees eighty thousands had he paid in public view, with further maneuvering needed to clinch control. Yet the acquisition is darkened by cruelty toward the women of the fort, so possession arrives with both status and curse.
This makes the page morally unstable in an important way. Success is real, but it is narrated through actions that also seed future decline and disrepute.
